atall: “The everloving Mister Crooms will gimme anything atall Ah wants.”
atavistic: Peter, strumming a haunting, atavistic measure; Joanna, dancing like a faun, instructed Maggie Ellersley.
atalanta: There were many songs of the fugitive like that which opens “The Wings of Atalanta,” and the more familiar “Been a-listening.

Perhaps Atlanta was not christened for the winged maiden of dull Boeotia; you know the tale,—how swarthy Atalanta, tall and wild, would marry only him who out-raced her; and how the wily Hippomenes laid three apples of gold in the way.
The Wings of Atalanta are the coming universities of the South.
And they say that yon gray mist is the tunic of Atalanta pausing over her golden apples.
If Atlanta be not named for Atalanta, she ought to have been.
How heavy a journey for weary feet! what wings must Atalanta have to flit over all this hollow and hill, through sour wood and sullen water, and by the red waste of sun-baked clay!
atalantas: Their faces were powdered and they caught up their dresses, when they touched earth, like alarmed Atalantas.
